subject: Order form: invoicing pathway, activation fee proration & tax evidence
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightarc.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@brightarc.com
Date: Tue, 28 May 2028 15:07:00 +0000
Subject: Redwood order form — invoicing cadence & tax handling

Mina,

Thanks for the draft order form. A few open items from procurement to make sure we can route payments cleanly across our finance teams: 

- How will the activation fee be invoiced and prorated if we start mid-month? We prefer a single activation invoice but need clarity on proration for month 1.
- Can invoices be split between our US entity and our EU entity (reverse-charge VAT)? If so, what evidence do you need for VAT reverse-charge and EU tax residency?
- We expect net 45 normally — can Redwood support net 45 for standard invoices and net 30 for activation/one-time fees?
- Please confirm whether deposits (if any) will be applied to the first monthly invoice or handled as a separate prepay credit.

We'd like to get this locked this week. Attaching a short procurement checklist (not a full redline yet).

—Samir
Samir Patel
Director, Procurement
BrightArc

Attachments: brightarc_procurement_checklist.pdf (stub)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightarc.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2028 17:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Redwood order form — invoicing cadence & tax handling

Samir — thanks, clear list. I pulled in Finance and Legal to confirm operationally. Summary of our proposed approach below; redline attached.

1) Activation fee proration: Redwood proposes a one-time activation invoice for 50% of the activation fee on contract execution and the remaining 50% net 30 after go-live. If start date is mid-month, monthly subscription in month 1 is prorated by days active; activation fee is not prorated further (it's a separate line item).

2) Deposits/prepay: Any deposit will be posted as a credit on your account and applied to the next invoice(s) until exhausted. We can alternatively issue a separate prepay invoice if your accounting requires it.

3) Invoice split by entity & VAT: We can split invoice lines across entities (US vs EU) but need the following evidence for reverse-charge/VAT handling: EU entity VAT number (VIES check), billing entity legal name and remit address, and a statement of tax residency. For US entities we need W-9 or equivalent.

4) Net terms: Standard is net 45 for subscription invoices; activation/one-time fees can be net 30 upon request. Any deviation to net 30 across the board will need commercial approval due to cashflow impact.

Attached: BrightArc_orderform_redline_v1.pdf (marked with the redline for activation fee and invoice split).

If agreeable, Finance will produce a sample invoice schedule and Kimberly will update the order form summary sheet. Jordan — any legal caveats on tax evidence wording?

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: BrightArc_orderform_redline_v1.pdf (redline stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 29 May 2028 09:33:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Redwood order form — invoicing cadence & tax handling

Looping in Finance thoughts — quick notes: 

- Applying deposit as an account credit is easiest for our billing system and avoids double-invoicing reconciliation on your side. We'll include a memo line: "Applied deposit: account credit" with dates.
- Activation fee split (50/50) is fine from cashflow perspective, but we need to log the second invoice as "activation completion" with a reference to the original PO number. Please confirm PO/PO-line mapping.
- Invoice split by legal entity: we can emit separate invoices per remit-to entity. However, we cannot apply a single line-item split across two invoices in our accounting system; each line must be assigned to a remit entity. If BrightArc needs a single combined view, we can provide a summary PDF consolidating the separate invoices.
- Net 45 standard is acceptable. If BrightArc requires net 30 for the activation balance, we will make an exception provided the PO explicitly references net 30 for that invoice.

I attached an example invoice_schedule_example.csv showing how we'd map line items to remit entities and invoice dates.

Ben Carter
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

Attachments: invoice_schedule_example.csv (stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightarc.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 29 May 2028 13:22:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Redwood order form — invoicing cadence & tax handling

Samir — appreciate the quick list. Two pragmatic concessions to accelerate execution: 

- We'll do activation fee 50/50 as Mina suggested. The first activation invoice will be issued on signature (net 30), second invoice issued at go-live (net 30). If you prefer the second at net 45, Ben already confirmed we'd accept that if the PO reflects it.
- For year 1 minimums: instead of a fixed annual minimum, we propose a "year-one usage threshold" equal to 60% of the committed run rate, with a true-up invoice at year-end if usage falls below the threshold. That gives BrightArc flexibility while protecting Redwood's revenue assumptions.

On evidence: For EU reverse-charge we only need the VAT number and a VIES lookup screenshot; for US remit we need the PO + remit-to entity name. For cross-entity billing please send the remit entity list and one sample PO per remit entity so Ben can map invoices.

If BrightArc can provide: 1) remit entities + VAT/W-9 evidence and 2) PO mapping by Friday, we'll prepare the final order form and DocuSign packet.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightarc.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@brightarc.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2028 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Redwood order form — invoicing cadence & tax handling

Thanks team — this all looks workable. We will: 

1) Provide remit entity list + VAT numbers and our US entity W-9 by EOD Friday.
2) Issue two POs: one for activation (PO-BA-1029) and one for subscription (PO-BA-1030) to reflect the invoice split.

Please confirm: once we send the documents, will Redwood regenerate the order form and send a DocuSign packet? If so, please include the invoice schedule (matching the CSV Ben provided) and a note that the activation second installment is tied to "activation completion" event.

Also, can you attach the minimal tax evidence wording Redwood expects, so we can include it with our submission?

If you can confirm the DocuSign link and expected signers, we will route OOB to procurement and legal on our side.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Director, Procurement
BrightArc
